# Lab 18.8: Data Governance Tags & IAM Conditions

## What We Are Going to Do
Attach Resource Manager tags to datasets and grant access with an IAM condition based on those tags, and compare tags with labels and policy tags.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a tag key and values.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud resource-manager tags keys create data_env --parent=projects/$PROJECT_ID
gcloud resource-manager tags values create prod --parent=$PROJECT_ID/data_env
gcloud resource-manager tags values create dev --parent=$PROJECT_ID/data_env</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Tag two datasets.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab18_prod
bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab18_dev
gcloud resource-manager tags bindings create --tag-value=$PROJECT_ID/data_env/prod \
  --parent=//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/$PROJECT_ID/datasets/lab18_prod --location=us
gcloud resource-manager tags bindings create --tag-value=$PROJECT_ID/data_env/dev \
  --parent=//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/$PROJECT_ID/datasets/lab18_dev --location=us</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[CLI] Grant access only to dev datasets.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=serviceAccount:$ANALYST \
  --role=roles/bigquery.dataEditor \
  --condition="expression=resource.matchTag('$PROJECT_ID/data_env', 'dev'),title=dev-only"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The analyst can edit any dataset tagged `dev`, now or in future, and nothing tagged `prod`.

4. **[Console] Compare three kinds of metadata.** Open `lab18_dev → Details`:
   - **Labels**: key-value pairs for billing and filtering. No access control.
   - **Tags**: Resource Manager tags. Can drive IAM conditions.
   - **Policy tags**: column-level classification for fine-grained access (Lab 18.5).

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Tag binding | Dataset tagged `prod` or `dev` |
| IAM condition | Access by tag, not by name |
| Labels | Cost reporting only |
| Policy tags | Column-level access |
